name: OMTech Polar 2 50W RF
tagline: Desktop RF CO₂: 2,000 mm/s engraving, air cooling and a 30,000-hour metal tube
tldr: The Polar 2 50W RF uses a metal RF CO₂ source instead of a glass tube: faster engraving (up to 2,000 mm/s with 2G acceleration), a 0.07 mm spot, air cooling and a rated life of up to 30,000 hours. Same 710 × 360 mm bed, 16 MP camera, auto-focus and rotary as the 70W glass version, for $1,300 more. Specs are OMTech's; no independent long-term review yet.
mainObjective: Fast, fine CO₂ engraving on a desktop bed with low maintenance

priceRange.note: OMTech store price (Oct 2026), list $7,599.99; package includes rotary, LightBurn key and exhaust kit

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm acrylic

cut: Clear and coloured acrylic up to ~8 mm (estimate)
cannot: Sheets longer than the bed (no pass-through)

pros: RF metal tube: much faster raster engraving and a finer 0.07 mm spot than glass-tube desktops
Air-cooled: no water loop to fill, monitor or protect from freezing
Tube rated up to 30,000 hours with a 24-month tube warranty
Same complete package as the 70W: 16 MP camera, auto-focus, air assist, exhaust fan, rotary, LightBurn key
cons: $1,300 more than the 70W glass version for less raw cutting power
No pass-through, so long sheets must be cut down first
Brand-new model: speed and precision figures are OMTech's, not yet independently tested
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 50W RF SKU of the Polar 2. Compare it with the 70W glass version: the lower wattage is not a downgrade in practice, since RF sources pulse faster and engrave finer. Choose it if engraving volume and low maintenance matter more than cutting thick stock.
proTips: Use the speed headroom for raster jobs, not for cutting: thick acrylic still wants slow passes. Keep the air filter and exhaust path clean, since the RF tube relies on air cooling. Verify camera alignment with a test mark before batch jobs.

faq.question: Why is the 50W RF more expensive than the 70W glass Polar 2?
faq.answer: RF metal tubes cost more to build. In exchange they pulse much faster for engraving, produce a finer spot, last up to about 30,000 hours (versus about 10,000 for glass) and are air-cooled. The 70W glass tube still cuts thicker material.

faq.question: Does the Polar 2 RF need water cooling?
faq.answer: No. OMTech lists it as air-cooled with no water tank, which removes the chiller, coolant and freezing concerns of glass tubes.

faq.question: Can the Polar 2 engrave metal?
faq.answer: Not bare metal: CO₂ wavelengths reflect off it. Anodized aluminum and coated metals mark well, and bare steel needs a marking compound or a fiber laser.

standoutFeatures.title: RF source for fast, fine engraving
standoutFeatures.body: Up to 2,000 mm/s with 2G acceleration and a spot of about 0.07 mm (OMTech figures). Photo fills and small text come out faster and crisper than on the glass-tube Polar 2.

standoutFeatures.title: Air-cooled, long-life tube
standoutFeatures.body: No water loop to fill, monitor or protect from frost. OMTech rates the RF tube for up to 30,000 hours and covers it for 24 months.

accessories.note: 16 MP full-bed camera, ±1 mm positioning (OMTech figure)
Integrated exhaust fan and pipe: duct it outside
LightBurn key in the OMTech package

editorialDepth.advantages: The RF Polar 2 is built for engraving volume: photo fills, logos on batches of coasters, detailed acrylic. Fast pulsing, a fine spot and air cooling make it a low-fuss machine for a small business that runs it every day.
editorialDepth.limitations: If most of your hours are spent cutting thick acrylic or plywood, the 70W glass version does more for less money. No pass-through, a footprint of about 1.2 m wide, and figures that still await independent testing.
